name: 2026-10-01-claude-964b-74769
note: Test helper edited with sed, then tests passed.

steps.title: Skip fetch-blocked ports in the test port picker
Ask Node which ports fetch refuses
Add 6679, rerun the server tests 15 times and the suite

body.command: cd /c/Dot; sed -i 's/const BLOCKED = new Set(\[6000, 6566, 6665, 6666, 6667, 6668, 6669, 6697\]);/const BLOCKED = new Set([6000, 6566, 6665, 6666, 6667, 6668, 6669, 6679, 6697]);/; s/(\\"bad port\\": 6000 X11, 6566, 6665-6669 IRC, 6697)/("bad port": 6000 X11, 6566, 6665-6669 IRC, 6679, 6697)/' test/server.test.js test/agents.test.js test/context.test.js; sed -i 's/6665-6669 IRC, 6697), like browsers do./6665-6669 IRC, 6679, 6697), like browsers do./' test/server.test.js test/agents.test.js test/context.test.js; grep -n "BLOCKED = \|bad port" test/server.test.js; fails=0; for i in $(seq 1 15); do out=$(timeout 120 node --test test/server.test.js 2>&1); if echo "$out" | grep -q "^ℹ fail 0"; then printf "."; else fails=$((fails+1)); printf "F"; fi; done; echo; echo "fails: $fails"; timeout 200 npm test > "$TEMP/t.out" 2>&1; grep -E "^ℹ (pass|fail)" "$TEMP/t.out"

steps.title: Push the fix and run CI twice

body.command:
cd /c/Dot; git add test/server.test.js test/agents.test.js test/context.test.js && git commit -q -m "test: skip the ports fetch refuses (\"bad port\": 6000, 6566, 6665-6669, 6679, 6697)

The tests started bridges on random ports from 5190 to 7190. Now and then one
landed on a port Node's fetch refuses outright, like browsers do, and the
first request failed with \"fetch failed\" (cause: bad port).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <[REDACTED:email]>" && git push -q origin next && sha=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) && echo "pushed $sha" && sleep 20 && ids=$(gh run list --branch next --limit 10 --json databaseId,headSha,workflowName --jq ".[] | select(.headSha | startswith(\"$sha\")) | select(.workflowName==\"CI\") | .databaseId") && echo "runs:" $ids && wait_all() { for i in $(seq 1 45); do pending=0; for id in $ids; do st=$(gh run view "$id" --json status --jq .status 2>/dev/null); [ "$st" != "completed" ] && pending=1; done; [ $pending = 0 ] && break; sleep 20; done; for id in $ids; do gh run view "$id" --json event,conclusion,jobs --jq '"\(.event): \(.conclusion) — " + ([.jobs[] | "\(.name | sub("Node ";"") | sub(" on ";"/")): \(.conclusion)"] | join(", "))'; done; }; wait_all; echo "=== second pass"; for id in $ids; do gh run rerun "$id" > /dev/null 2>&1; done; sleep 30; wait_all

steps.title: Check what the same-file warning actually does

body.command: cd /c/Dot; grep -n "^export function overlaps" -B6 bridge/ui/story.js | head -10; s=$(grep -n "^export function overlaps" bridge/ui/story.js | cut -d: -f1); sed -n "$s,$((s+20))p" bridge/ui/story.js | grep -n "30\|session\|change" | head -8

end.title: Finished
end.summary:
est helper now skips those ports. dotpals itself always uses port 5175, so users were never affected.
